findings.fact: Before initial mount: revalidate exact state partition identity, parent, UUID, type, idle state and GPT; raw journal containment; require original BLKROGET=0; claim flag ownership before potentially ambiguous ioctl; set RO and verify BLKROGET=1; revalidate identity again. No SD block flag is changed.

Raw parser reads at most 236 bytes from primary superblock offset 1024, validates each token as decimal byte 0..255, and requires exactly 236 bytes. Checks magic bytes 0x53/0xef, HAS_JOURNAL compat bit4, absence of JOURNAL_DEV incompat bit8, all 16 external journal UUID bytes zero, full LE32 journal inode exactly8, and all four journal device bytes zero. Bytewise checks avoid host endianness and shell 32-bit arithmetic issues. Orphan fields may remain nonzero intentionally because the probe is block protected.

Initial state marker, directories and machine-id are checked while selected partition is block RO. A failed marker check aborts handoff; cleanup may restore only original block writability after unmount and revalidation, but never attempts a writable filesystem mount or bypasses marker validation.

RO release requires same identity/parent/UUID/ext4, no mounts or holders, GPT and raw internal-journal guard, original flag0 and current confirmed flag1. Refused identity, busy mount, malformed inventory or journal containment prevents setrw. Failed unmount cannot be bypassed by clearing HI_MOUNTS because production hs_idle checks kernel mountinfo independently.

After release, writability plus target identity/UUID/idle/GPT/raw journal guard are rechecked before authorized RW recovery; marker and machine-id are checked again after recovery. A setrw verification failure aborts before RW filesystem mounting.

RO ownership is cleared only after successful setrw verification. /run move and subsequent runtime setup are reachable only after this clear, so late cleanup cannot accidentally clear another block flag. Existing moved mount tracking unmounts state at /newroot/run/a733-state; failure restore paths still rely on actual major:minor mountinfo.

primary_sources.facts: Lines 393-424 skip cleanup only if no legacy orphan/no orphan-file blocks, block device RO, unsupported RW features or existing filesystem error. Otherwise even SB_RDONLY is temporarily cleared. Lines 455-489 process list/file orphans; line 508 restores original flags. Lines 583-593 initialize orphan-file blocks when compat feature exists.

NOLOAD controls journal initialization at 5397; orphan info initialization 5587 and cleanup 5606 are separate later operations. Therefore noload does not suppress orphan cleanup. Error handler at 725-736 commits error information if block device writable even for an RO mount; sb_rdonly return is at 749.

Superblock little-endian feature masks are at 0x5c/0x60/0x64, journal UUID/inum/dev at 0xd0/0xe0/0xe4, legacy s_last_orphan at 0xe8. Compat ORPHAN_FILE=0x1000 at line 2006; RO_COMPAT_ORPHAN_PRESENT=0x10000 at 2027.

Mount-options documentation describes ro,noload for preventing writes and warns that skipping recovery on an unclean filesystem exposes inconsistencies. Pinned implementation above gives the more specific orphan/error-path behavior.

hi_state mounts ro,noload, validates directories/marker/machine-id, unmounts, revalidates identity/UUID/idle/GPT, then mounts RW for journal recovery and revalidates state.

Resolver itself uses blkid -p and identity/idle/GPT checks without mounting. It requires writable STATE eligibility, so its read-only name does not imply block-level RO. No raw internal-journal/orphan guard is present.

Raw validation already restricts target geometry and incompat mask 0x2c6, has_journal, journal UUID zero/inum8/dev0. It lacks legacy and file-orphan guards. Counters checked after unmount detect changes after the event; refusal cannot undo a mount-induced write.

Default plan is unmounted and read-only. Apply explicitly mounts RW before in-filesystem checks and raw validator currently checks only UUID/label/magic. This is a separately authorized write helper, not proof that journal containment is safe; preserve/widen raw internal-journal guard before its first RW mount too.

before_any_mount: Preserve all existing fixed-device, quiescent-RAM, geometry, incompat-feature and internal-journal checks.
Read exactly 1024-byte primary superblock from partition offset 1024 through verified O_RDONLY descriptor. Require LE32 at offset 232 (0xe8), s_last_orphan, == 0.

For narrow supported policy require (LE32 at 92 & 0x1000)==0 and (LE32 at 100 & 0x10000)==0; refusing ORPHAN_PRESENT alone is insufficient because cleanup visits allocated orphan-file blocks without testing that bit.

Do not conflate RECOVER bit 0x4 with orphan safety. noload suppresses journal replay; allowing RECOVER with no orphan metadata retains the existing best-effort unjournalled export semantics. Refusing RECOVER as an additional conservative policy is valid but rejects more useful crash exports.
Revalidate identity and raw guard immediately before mount in the quiescent environment. Keep post-unmount counters as evidence.
exporter_guard_recommendation.strict_zero_write_requirement: These guards close observed orphan-cleanup paths, not arbitrary ext4-corruption/error writes. For an unconditional nonwriting-source promise require verified block-device RO protection throughout mounting/traversal/unmount, or use a verified RO copy and mount only the copy. Do not automatically repair or fall back to RW after refusal.
exporter_guard_recommendation.preserve_external_journal_protection: has_journal required; journal UUID all zero; inode8; journal_dev0; JOURNAL_DEV incompat excluded. Enforce this before any writable mount, not after mountinfo inspection.

boot_options.effect: Add raw pre-mount guard; orphan state reaches recovery shell without probing the filesystem. Requires reviewed recovery procedure to regain boot after such a crash; preserve authorized write target and validate marker safely before RW recovery.

After exact identity/idle/internal-journal validation, save p4 RO state, set and verify block-level RO using a packaged/tested primitive, then ro,noload probe and verify mount identity and STATE marker/machine-id. Unmount normally and prove no owned mount remains. Revalidate same node major:minor/parent/UUID/internal-journal/GPT/idle, restore write eligibility for that same p4 only, verify it, then perform existing authorized RW recovery and post-replay state checks. Any verification/unmount failure stops handoff; never clear RO on an uncertain device. No SD RO flag changes or SD writes.

Preserve raw source through verified read-only access to independent storage, inspect/recover only owned copy first. Requires capacity/tools and explicit evidence separation; do not mount original RW before source identity/marker verification.

meaningful_tests: Unit cases: valid clean + RECOVER-only with last_orphan0 allowed under chosen policy; reject s_last_orphan values 1 and 0xffffffff; reject orphan_file even with ORPHAN_PRESENT clear; reject ORPHAN_PRESENT alone; retain external UUID/inum/dev/JOURNAL_DEV exclusions. Assert mount function never called on refused input.

Owned-file/loop regression: construct disposable ext4 with valid checksum and a legacy orphan entry (or reproducible abrupt-stop image), prove production preflight refuses before mount and full source SHA256/write sectors remain unchanged. Existing clean loop test does not exercise this case.

For block-RO option, on only a newly owned loop containing orphan state: verify BLKROGET=1 before ro,noload mount, marker read and normal unmount, no source changes; deliberate wrong marker must cause zero RW attempts. Then restore only known loop eligibility and separately exercise validated RW journal recovery.

findings.evidence: LE32 offset24=2 selects 4096-byte blocks. Offset4=PART_SIZE/4096 and offset336=0 enforce exact 8 GiB filesystem count, including high word. Existing 8 GiB partition/block ioctl guards remain unchanged.

has_journal bit4 required. Python precedence makes not u32(96) & ~0x2c6 reject every incompat bit outside the mask. Exhaustive single-bit synthetic check accepted only bit indexes 1,2,6,7,9. JOURNAL_DEV bit3 is excluded. RECOVER bit2 remains permitted.

Requires all 16 journal UUID bytes zero, LE32 journal inode=8 and LE32 journal_dev=0 before mount, preventing external-journal redirection. No orphan refusal added, appropriately retaining sanctioned RW replay/cleanup behavior.

Production inspect_target reads raw p4 superblock through O_RDONLY verified fd and validates it. execute calls inspect_target initially and again on apply after repeating runtime/archive guards; neither mountpoint creation nor RW mount occurs until both return matching identity. Subsequent mountinfo check remains in place.

Seven distinct journal/feature failures are tested through both apply preflights, asserting expected inspection count and no tempfile/mount subprocess calls. Fixture calls production raw validator; mocked inspect_target isolates hardware while source review confirms real wiring. Positive dirty RECOVER plus legacy/file-orphan metadata remains allowed.
